headline: Work has started on a $15 billion data centre campus on desert land in Hudspeth County, Texas, and the county judge says local officials were not told beforehand.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered to 5: groundbreaking was on Wed 7 Oct 2026, before the window; the figures are company claims relayed by one local station.
importance_line: Residents of Hudspeth County have little say over a campus on about 24,000 acres that would draw on a local aquifer, because Texas counties cannot zone private land, and the water and power plans come from the developers and are not independently checked.
summary: KTSM 9 News reports that Los Angeles-based Kaufman & Company and partners broke ground on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026 near Desert Haven, where Boise-based ServerDomes says the campus will generate its own 350 megawatts, enough for at least 100,000 homes, and draw well water only once before recycling it. County Judge Joanna MacKenzie says no local authority was told beforehand and that "local government should be included in that conversation", but Texas counties cannot zone private land, so the planners have agreed only to present the project on 27 Oct.
notes: Read at EverythingLubbock.com, a Nexstar station site carrying KTSM's own text; credit goes to KTSM 9 News. Original KTSM link not found.
